extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, Medicare policy stakeholders, Medicare Administrative Contractors (MACs), actuaries, and other commenters on the FY 2027 IPPS/LTCH PPS proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Federal guidance for calculating uncompensated care payments under section 1886(r) for IPPS/LTCH hospitals for FY 2027, including the definitions and computation of Factors 1–3, data sources, trims, exclusions, new/merged hospital policies, and scaling adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 1 definition (statutory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor 1 is the difference between the Secretary's estimates of: (1) the amount that would have been paid in Medicare DSH payments for the fiscal year in the absence of section 1886(r); and (2) the amount of empirically justified Medicare DSH payments that are made for the fiscal year (which takes into account the requirement to pay 25 percent of what would have otherwise been paid under section 1886(d)(5)(F)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY 2027, CMS determines Factor 1 from OACT's most recently available estimates of aggregate Medicare DSH payments without regard to section 1886(r)(1) and the aggregate amount of empirically justified Medicare DSH payments (25 percent). For this proposed rule CMS used OACT's January 2026 estimates based on the December 2025 HCRIS extract and the FY 2026 IPPS Impact File. Consistent with past practice, these proposed-rule estimates will not be revised after publication of the final projections in the FY 2027 final rule, although OACT intends to use more recent data where available for the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of OACT estimates and non-revision policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor 1 and related projections are determined from OACT estimates and, historically, proposed-rule Factor 1 estimates are not revised or updated after publication of final projections in the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OACT's projections use most recently filed Medicare hospital cost reports with DSH information, the IPPS Impact File adjustments, and OACT's Part A benefits projection model (discharges, utilization, case-mix). Factor 1 estimates are generally consistent with President's Budget assumptions and Midsession Review analyses; Midsession Review updates may inform final Factor 1. CMS will include data sources, methods, assumptions, and components of update factors in the preamble and invites comments on proposed Factor 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from OACT DSH estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain hospitals are excluded from OACT's Medicare DSH estimates used to calculate Factor 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY 2027, CMS excluded SCHs paid under hospital-specific rates (ineligible for empirically justified Medicare DSH and uncompensated care payments), Maryland hospitals (not paid under IPPS), and 22 hospitals participating in the Rural Community Hospital Demonstration Program (ineligible under demonstration payment methodology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 2 definition (statutory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor 2 is 1 minus the percent change in the percent of individuals who are uninsured, comparing the percent uninsured in 2013 and the percent uninsured in the most recent period for which data are available, as estimated by the Secretary and certified by the Chief Actuary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY 2027, CMS continues to use the National Health Expenditure Accounts (NHEA) to measure the rate of uninsurance and uses a weighted-average approach to map calendar-year NHEA rates to the fiscal year (so the FY uninsured rate reflects the fiscal-year experience). OACT projected uninsured rates for CY 2026 and CY 2027 and certified the estimates; the proposed Factor 2 calculation is 1−((0.14−0.091)/0.14)=0.65 (65.00 percent). CMS may consider more recent data before finalizing Factor 2 and invites public comment on the proposed Factor 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of NHEA as data source for Factor 2
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS uses the NHEA for estimates of uninsured rates because it provides comprehensive, official government estimates of health sector spending and enrollment, including uninsured counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NHEA includes estimates for private insurance types, Medicare, Medicaid, CHIP, other public programs, and uninsured individuals; OACT's NHEA-based projections (most recent projection window 2024–2033 using NHEA historical data through 2023) are the basis for projected uninsured rates used in Factor 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted-average approach for fiscal-year uninsured rate
rubrics_metrics.description: To estimate the rate of uninsurance during a fiscal year, CMS applies a weighted average of the calendar year estimates spanning the fiscal year rather than using a single calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach was originally adopted in FY 2014 and is continued for FY 2027 so Factor 2 reflects the uninsured rate hospitals experience during the fiscal year. OACT certified the weighted-average approach for FY 2027 and CMS may use more recent NHEA data before the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 3 definition (statutory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor 3 is the hospital-specific percent that equals the quotient of: (1) the amount of uncompensated care for the hospital for a period selected by the Secretary (numerator), and (2) the aggregate amount of uncompensated care for all subsection (d) hospitals that receive a payment under section 1886(r) for such period (denominator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factor 3 expresses each hospital's share of estimated uncompensated care among all DSH-eligible hospitals and is applied to the product of Factor 1 and Factor 2 to determine each eligible hospital's uncompensated care payment. The statute permits use of alternative data if it is a better proxy for costs of treating uninsured individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-year average for Factor 3 (audited Worksheet S-10 data)
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY 2024 and subsequent years, CMS uses a 3‑year average of uncompensated care data from the 3 most recent fiscal years for which audited Worksheet S-10 cost report data are available to determine Factor 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY 2023 used a 2‑year average (FYs 2018 and 2019); three-year averaging was finalized to smooth year-to-year fluctuations. If a hospital lacks data for all 3 years, CMS averages the hospital's available data. IHS/Tribal and Puerto Rico hospitals are included in the multi-year average policy. For FY 2027 CMS uses audited FYs 2021, 2022, and 2023 S-10 data (December 2025 HCRIS extract).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim payments with final cost report settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS makes interim uncompensated care and empirically justified Medicare DSH payments and reconciles them at final cost report settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MAC will make final determinations regarding a hospital's eligibility for DSH payments and uncompensated care payments at cost report settlement. Interim payments are based on projections available at rule development time; final adjustments occur at settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scaling factor to reconcile multi-year Factor 3 sums
rubrics_metrics.description: When Factor 3 is calculated using multiple years of data, CMS applies a scaling factor so the total uncompensated care payments to projected DSH-eligible hospitals equal the estimated total available for the fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute scaling factor as: divide 1 (the expected sum of Factor 3 values) by the actual sum of all DSH-eligible hospitals' Factor 3 values, then multiply that quotient by each hospital's uncompensated care payment to obtain scaled payments. This ensures consistency between individual Factor 3 allocations and the total uncompensated care amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: New hospital policy for Factor 3
rubrics_metrics.description: New hospitals (no cost report data for the most recent year used in Factor 3) are treated specially in the Factor 3 calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New hospitals may receive interim empirically justified DSH payments if preliminarily projected DSH-eligible, but will not receive interim uncompensated care payments (no S-10 data). For FY 2027, hospitals with CCNs established on or after October 1, 2023, are 'new.' CMS determines the numerator using the new hospital's uncompensated care costs on its current-year S‑10, uses a denominator based on uncompensated care costs from the most recent fiscal year with audits, and applies the scaling factor to the new hospital's Factor 3. Final eligibility/payment determined at cost report settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newly merged hospital policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Hospitals that merge after development of the final rule are treated similarly to new hospitals for Factor 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final uncompensated care payment for the newly merged hospital is determined at cost report settlement; numerator based on the surviving hospital's (newly merged hospital's) cost report for the current fiscal year. If the cost reporting period has <12 months, data are annualized. Denominator uses uncompensated care costs from most recent audited fiscal year for projected DSH-eligible hospitals. A scaling factor is applied, and interim payments for the newly merged hospital are based only on data for the surviving hospital's CCN available at final rule development.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCR trim methodology (5-step process)
rubrics_metrics.description: To calculate uncompensated care costs on Worksheet S-10, CMS trims cost-to-charge ratios (CCRs) through a multi-step process to avoid aberrant CCRs skewing statewide averages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 1: Remove Maryland hospitals and all-inclusive rate providers. Step 2: Compute CCR for each remaining hospital (total costs Line 202 Col 3 divided by charges Line 202 Col 8); calculate CCR ceiling as 3 standard deviations above the national geometric mean CCR and remove hospitals exceeding the ceiling. Step 3: Compute urban and rural statewide average CCRs weighted by total hospital discharges (Worksheet S-3) for the applicable fiscal year. Step 4: Assign statewide average CCR to hospitals with CCRs > 3 std dev above national geometric mean (i.e., those above the ceiling). Step 5: For hospitals without a reported CCR on S-10 Line 1, assign the statewide average CCR. After trimming, recalculate hospital uncompensated care costs (Line 30) using the trimmed CCR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uncompensated Care Costs (UCC) trim methodology for aberrant UCC
rubrics_metrics.description: If a hospital's uncompensated care costs for any fiscal year included in the multi-year average are an extremely high ratio (>50%) of its total operating costs, CMS applies an adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will determine the ratio of uncompensated care costs to total operating costs from another available cost report and apply that ratio to total operating expenses for the potentially aberrant year to compute an adjusted UCC amount. However, if the hospital's UCC data for that fiscal year have been audited, CMS will not apply the UCC trim (audited data carry increased confidence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative trim for high insured patients' charity care
rubrics_metrics.description: For some hospitals without audited S-10 data, CMS applies an alternative trim targeting potentially aberrant insured patients' charity care costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY 2023 and subsequent years, if a hospital's insured patients' charity care costs for a fiscal year exceed $7 million and the ratio of cost of insured patient charity care (S-10 line 23 col 2) to total uncompensated care costs (line 30) is greater than 60 percent, CMS will not calculate a Factor 3 for that hospital at the time of proposed or final rulemaking. This trim affects only hospitals not currently projected to be DSH-eligible (thus not part of the denominator). If a hospital would be trimmed under both the UCC trim and this alternative trim, CMS applies the alternative trim instead. If a hospital subject to this trim is later determined DSH-eligible at cost report settlement, the MAC will calculate Factor 3 using the new-hospital methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thresholds for identifying potentially aberrant insured charity care data
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS uses statistical and dollar thresholds to identify potentially aberrant insured patient charity care data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS applies a threshold of 3 standard deviations from the mean ratio of insured patients' charity care costs to total UCC (line 23 col 2 divided by line 30) and a dollar threshold equal to the median total UCC reported on the most recent audited cost reports for hospitals projected to be DSH-eligible. CMS continued to apply the threshold amounts originally calculated for FY 2019 for FY 2025 and subsequent fiscal years to promote transparency and predictability. Worksheet S-10 data from IHS/Tribal and Puerto Rico hospitals are included in this approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on using audited Worksheet S-10 data before expanding multi-year averaging
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS will use multi-year averages for Factor 3 only when the vast majority of providers have audited S‑10 data for more than one fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenter concerns about year-to-year variation led CMS to move from single-year to multi-year averaging once audited data availability (e.g., audited FY 2020 reports) supported it. Lessons learned from audits inform the audit process and trimming decisions; audited data reduce the need for certain trims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of specific data extracts and years for FY 2027 Factor 3
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the FY 2027 proposed rule, CMS will calculate Factor 3 using the most recent 3 years of audited cost reports: FYs 2021, 2022, and 2023, using reports from the December 2025 HCRIS extract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will apply the scaling factor, new hospital, newly merged hospital, CCR trim, UCC trim, and alternative trim policies discussed in the preamble when calculating Factor 3 for FY 2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projection methodology components for estimating Medicare DSH expenditures
rubrics_metrics.description: OACT's projection of Medicare DSH payments applies multiple update factors to a baseline (e.g., FY 2023) to estimate expenditures for future fiscal years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OACT starts with a baseline (e.g., $12.901 billion for FY 2023) and applies factors including discharges (adjusted by completion factors for recent years and assumptions for later years, accounting for MA enrollment), case-mix (based on claims data and historical panels for future years), 'Other' (differences between total inpatient and IPPS discharges and various payment rate adjustments), and the IPPS Hospital Market Basket Update Factor. CMS describes the assumptions and rationales for each component and invites comment on Factor 1 driven by these projections.
